_comment: Authored interview prompts. Tones: self_deprecating, honest, confident, absurd, roast. Each prompt's tone_mods add to the set-result modifiers in balancing.interview.tone_by_set_result. Conditions: background, job, hook, min_appearances, max_appearances, housing, min_day.

prompts.text: So where are you from, and why would you leave?

responses.text: Somewhere small enough that I'm already famous there for leaving.
I wanted to be a comedian, and my hometown has one stage. It's a tractor.
Honestly? I needed to find out if I'm any good.
I'm from wherever you're about to roast me about.

prompts.text: What do you do for money? Because it isn't this.

responses.text: Whatever pays this week. Today it's that.
I'm basically a professional apologizer with a tray.
I'm between fortunes.
More than your band, judging by their shoes.

prompts.text: You wait tables? What's the worst order you've ever taken?

responses.text: Eggs with no yolk and no white. I brought her a plate. She loved it.
Anything ordered by a man in a visor.
I'm the worst order. They keep sending me back.

prompts.text: You work a door? So you're the guy who decides who gets in.

responses.text: Yeah. And none of the panel would make it past me.
I check IDs. One guy's photo was an oil painting.
It's mostly counting. I'm decent at counting.

prompts.text: Delivery guy, huh? Ever eat someone's order?

responses.text: Once. They rated me one star and said I needed it more. They were right.
Never. I'm a professional.
Only the fries. Fries are a tax.

prompts.text: How long have you been doing comedy?

responses.text: A few weeks. You could probably tell.
A few weeks, but I've been funny my whole life.
Since the bus dropped me off. I counted.

prompts.text: You're back! What's changed since last time?

responses.text: I wrote new jokes. Most of them are still in the notebook, scared.
Everything. I've been writing every day.
I moved from the top bunk to the bottom bunk. Huge.

prompts.text: Where are you living right now?

responses.text: A hostel with eleven strangers and one guy who's legally part of the building.
Somewhere I can afford, which is nowhere.
With a roommate. You'd hate him. He's your biggest fan.

prompts.text: You've got a real stage presence. Theater kid?

responses.text: I played a teapot for eleven performances. I still pour when I'm nervous.
Guilty. Community theater. It shows.
Yes, and I'm the best actor on this stage. Low bar.

prompts.text: You look like you could throw somebody out. You a bouncer?

responses.text: Used to be. Hecklers here are nothing compared to a bachelorette party.
I'm actually very gentle. Ask anyone I carried out.
Don't make me prove it on the band.

prompts.text: Do your parents know you're up here tonight?

responses.text: My dad thinks I'm in the standing industry.
They're watching. Hi Mom. Sorry.
They're more nervous than I am.

prompts.text: What did you do before comedy?

responses.text: Software QA. I found bugs. Now I am one.
I tested apps. I gave your favorite one a two-star review.
I got laid off by an algorithm. It said I wasn't funny enough.

prompts.text: What's the dream? Where do you want to be in five years?

responses.text: Selling out arenas. And choosing my own openers.
Anywhere with a door that locks.
Sitting where you are, being mean to someone like me.
I'm great. That was my plan. Lower expectations.
Honestly, I froze. I'll be back.
The crowd was off tonight.

prompts.text: Okay, that was actually really good. Where did that come from?

responses.text: From bombing at the Rusty Spur about forty times.
I know. I've been waiting for you to notice.
I stole it from the band.

prompts.text: What's the weirdest thing you've seen since you got to Austin?

responses.text: A food truck in an ambulance. The siren means your tacos are ready.
People applauding bats. I'd kill for that reception.
Honestly? This show.

prompts.text: You keep coming back. Are you trying to become a regular?

responses.text: I'm trying to become furniture. Just leave me here.
Yes. That's the whole plan.
I'm trying to become a person who doesn't have to put my name in a bucket.

prompts.text: What's the worst gig you've ever done?

responses.text: A Tuesday open mic where the only audience was a man asleep with his eyes open.
I don't have bad gigs. I have learning experiences.
This one, so far. No offense to the band.
